column1: # tools/fuzz_coverage_floors.tsv: the sdk lines each fuzz target's replay must cover, per OS
# (tools/check_fuzz_coverage.py, run at the end of tools/fuzz_coverage.sh).
# Columns (tab-separated): target, os (uname -s: Linux or Darwin), min_lines or off.
#   min_lines: nine tenths of the sdk lines the target covered over its committed corpus and
#     2000 random inputs (the script's defaults; the night's campaign corpora only add to it),
#     rounded down. The tenth is a margin, not a measurement: a target under its floor is a
#     harness that reaches less than it did; read why before moving the floor.
#   off: the harness is compiled out on that OS (a Linux-only parser); it must cover 0 lines.
#   all: the union of every target.
# Measured 2026-11-12. Linux: hetzner2, branch ci/v1.1.8/checks-that-check at 9bb116638 with
# ROCKETNET_XDP on (Ubuntu clang 21.1.8). Darwin: macbook, the same tree, XDP off (Apple clang 21.0.0);
# the netlink and io_uring harnesses are Linux parsers and the XDP filter driver is not built.
# A target with no row for the OS it runs on is refused.
# rocketnet_fuzz_session_raw, 2026-11-12, the rebased end-to-end-checks tree: Linux bench-nyc-1 (Ubuntu clang 21.1.8,
# XDP on) covered 12956; Darwin macbook (Apple clang 21.0.0) covered 10247. Nine tenths, rounded down.
